html:
The Barranbinya are an Aboriginal Australian people of northern New South Wales, on the Barwon and Darling rivers between Brewarrina and Bourke. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them in detail. Nearby, at Brewarrina, stand the Brewarrina fish traps, a large network of stone weirs and pens across the river that people of the region used and shared, said to have been made by Baiame. Neighbours on the map include the Gunu, the Muruwari and the Wailwan. Paddle steamers on the Darling made Bourke a wool port from the 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
